decisions.stem: During a routine adolescent review, a parent says, "My 15-year-old can explain why risky dares are dangerous, but still does reckless things with friends." Which explanation best matches the note-based model of adolescent risk-taking?
A GP is helping a 13-year-old recover after major family stress. Which single protective factor is most clearly identified in the notes as supporting adolescent resilience?

A 15-year-old asks why the paediatrician is asking about home, school, peers, alcohol, sex, mood, sleep, safety, spirituality, and social media during a review for abdominal pain. What is the best explanation?
Parents of a 12-year-old ask how to set limits without damaging independence. Which advice best matches the parenting approach described in the notes?
Which adolescent is most clearly in a group that the notes say may have poorer health outcomes because of isolation and marginalisation?

A 14-year-old has no trusted adult outside the immediate family, feels school is pointless, has dropped all outside activities, and says, "Nothing I do changes anything." Which interpretation is best?
During HEEADSS, a 15-year-old says she has lost interest in friends and sometimes thinks "it would be easier not to wake up." Which HEEADSS area must be explored directly today?
A 14-year-old's HEEADSS review shows worsening school disengagement and no activities outside home. Which follow-up goal best aligns with the resilience factors highlighted in the notes?

A clinic team describes a stressed parent of a young person with a long-term condition as "hopeless" after several missed appointments. Which response best matches the notes on supporting parents in the health system?
A 13-year-old increasingly wants private time in clinic and more say in daily routines. Which parental response is most consistent with the developmental tasks of adolescence described in the notes?

A 16-year-old can think abstractly, compare several possible futures, and reason in more than one dimension, but is still vulnerable to risk-taking and poor regulation of affect. Which stage of adolescence best fits?
A 15-year-old is increasingly working out personal values, autonomy, and responsibility rather than simply copying family views. Which developmental task domain is most directly illustrated?
